fields.headline: PARAVISION GETS $6.5M STATE DEPARTMENT DEAL
fields.deck: The contract starts at $1.3 million and could run through 2031.

stories.caption:
The State Department has awarded Paravision, a facial recognition developer, a contract worth up to $6.5 million, according to federal procurement records. The award was made September 23 with an initial obligation of $1.3 million.

The firm-fixed-price deal can run through September 22, 2031. It was competed under simplified acquisition procedures as a total small-business set-aside, and only one offer was received.

Public award records do not name the Paravision products the department bought. The contract's "digital detection/identity assurance" description overlaps with the deepfake and synthetic-face detection tools Paravision markets, but the record does not show whether the award covers those tools, its liveness detection, its facial recognition or other software. A separate $24,717 purchase order for a software license, issued April 30, does not show whether it was linked to the September award.

Source: Biometric Update, 17 October 2026

Image: Biometric Update (courtesy)

📍San Diego, CA

Tech: Autonomous surveillance

Platform: Unmanned surface vessel

Goal: Provide persistent surveillance to detect illegal maritime activity, including drug trafficking and unauthorized vessel movement.

Why: Crewed patrols are limited by crew endurance, operating cost and the area one asset can cover at a time.

Traction: Lightfish fleet deployed in the Gulf of America in support of U.S. maritime border security, per Seasats. Vessels have operated on the Rio Grande since January 2026 for federal border security efforts.

Seasats said a fleet of Lightfish vessels has been deployed in the Gulf of America to support U.S. maritime border security, building on an autonomous surveillance effort already run for the Homeland Defense and Americas Security Affairs office in the Assistant Secretary of War's organization. The vessels launch from the Texas coast and run without a crew aboard.

Each Lightfish is roughly 11 feet long and 340 pounds, solar powered, and capable of multi-month endurance on station. Seasats says two people can launch and recover one from a boat ramp or a pickup truck. Its payload bay can be swapped between electro-optical and infrared cameras, signals gear and sonar, so one hull can be set up for the job at hand.

Assistant Secretary of War Mark R. Ditlevson said the work is part of efforts to "gain 100% operational control of our borders." The deployment is the company's latest step after Rio Grande operations that began in January 2026.

fields.headline: XTEND WINS $40.5M FOR 6,000 STRIKERS
fields.deck: The order follows a top-performer finish in Gauntlet II of the Drone Dominance Program.

frames.mediaQuery: STRIKER drone XTEND official company imagery

stories.caption:
XTEND AI Robotics (NYSE: XTND) has won a $40.5 million order for 6,000 STRIKER drones. The award comes after the company was named a top performer in the Close Quarters Battle segment of Gauntlet II, part of the U.S. Department of War's iterative $1 billion Drone Dominance Program.

STRIKER runs on XTEND's proprietary XOS operating system and is built for tactical missions in confined, complex and GNSS-denied environments. XTEND CEO Aviv Shapira said, "We competed, we proved our capabilities, and now we are ready to build."

Under the program's structure, Gauntlet II top performers skip the open solicitation and Pitch & Fly stages and move straight to Gauntlet III in the mission set where they were selected, after first fulfilling a 400-system production order. Gauntlet III performance will decide whether any Phase 3 orders are placed, and the company notes that taking part does not guarantee an award.

XTEND also released preliminary third quarter 2026 revenue and a backlog update. Those figures are company-reported and are not covered here.

Source: XTEND AI Robotics via Business Wire, 13 October 2026

fields.headline: ARMY TO TEST COUNTER-DRONE GEAR IN AFRICA
fields.deck: Africa trials aim to deliver field-ready systems to Soldiers within 180 days.

frames.mediaQuery: U.S. Army counter-unmanned aircraft systems Africa SETAF-AF

stories.caption:
The U.S. Army Southern European Task Force, Africa (SETAF-AF) is working with the service's Global Tactical Edge Acquisition Directorate (G-TEAD) to put emerging systems through trials in Africa, with the aim of delivering them to Soldiers within 180 days.

The first accelerated capability event (ACE) is set for spring 2027 in Tan-Tan, Morocco. It targets counter-unmanned aircraft systems and force protection, focusing on how to shield early-entry command posts and operating locations from Group 1–3 small UAS. The Army says Africa's open spectrum and uncongested airspace let Soldiers validate solutions in theater, conditions that U.S. and European training ranges struggle to match.

Each ACE moves through three phases: submission and preparation, Soldier-led demonstrations, and follow-on operational evaluation. The Soldier-led demonstration is planned for February and March 2027 in Tan-Tan, with a later assessment in the spring of 2027 during African Lion. G-TEAD will validate up to 15 solutions with PAE Fires as the transition partner.

Source: U.S. Army, October 16, 2026

Image: U.S. Army photo by Sgt. 1st Class Rodney Roldan

The appearance of U.S. Department of War (DoW) visual information does not imply or constitute DoW endorsement.

fields.headline: OFFICE OFFERS ANTHEIA UP TO $80M LOAN
fields.deck: The conditional loan would help Antheia onshore critical drug ingredients.

stories.caption:
The Department of War's Office of Strategic Capital has issued a conditional commitment for a direct, long-term loan of up to $80 million to Antheia, an advanced biosynthesis company. Alongside additional private capital, the financing would support Antheia's plan to move production of critical pharmaceutical ingredients to U.S. manufacturing.

Most of the key starting materials and active pharmaceutical ingredients the country depends on come from overseas, a gap that exposes patients to drug shortages during emergencies, disasters and supply disruptions. Antheia says it has previously received $32 million in non-dilutive federal financing, plus equity from strategic government-affiliated investors.

The commitment is conditional. Antheia must still meet financial, legal, technical, investment and due diligence requirements before financial close, and no financial close has been announced.

Source: Antheia via PR Newswire, Oct. 18, 2026
